rule: S_N must not be null
rationale: S_N serves as the primary identifier and one-to-one join key with Acc_Info_dirty. While no nulls are currently observed, this is a mandatory field for referential integrity.

rule: Every S_N in Cust_Bio_dirty must exist in Acc_Info_dirty.S_N
rationale: S_N is defined as a one-to-one shared join key with Acc_Info_dirty. Referential integrity must be enforced to ensure all records have corresponding matches in the sibling table.

rule: Account_No must not be null
rationale: Account_No is a mandatory business identifier for customer accounts. No missing values observed, but field is required by design.

rule: Account_No must be a 4-digit numeric code (e.g., 1026)
rationale: Evidence indicates Account_No should be treated as a string identifier with exactly 4 digits (range 1001-1028 observed).

rule: Account_No values must be unique
rationale: Account identifiers should uniquely identify accounts. Evidence shows 2 duplicate values (1001 and 1010) appearing in multiple records.

rule: Name must be in Title Case format (e.g., 'Wang Shi Jie'), not all-caps or all-lowercase
rationale: Sample contains case deviations: 'WANG SHI JIE' (all caps) and 'lim wei jie' (all lower). Standard naming convention requires Title Case, excluding known lowercase particles (bin, binte, d/o, s/o).

check_params.logic: any((w.isupper() or (len(w) > 0 and w[0].islower())) for w in str(row['Name']).split() if w.lower() not in ('bin','binte','d/o','s/o') and len(w) > 1)

rule: ID_No must not be null
rationale: National ID number is a mandatory identity verification field. No missing values observed.

rule: ID_No must follow Singapore NRIC format: one prefix letter (S/T/F/G), followed by exactly 7 digits, ending with one checksum letter (e.g., S1234567D)
rationale: 93.3% of values follow this 9-character pattern. Non-conforming values like '1916569C' (missing prefix) and 'F212233V' (6 digits) must be flagged.

rule: ID_No values must be unique
rationale: National ID numbers should uniquely identify individuals. Evidence shows duplicate value 'F1011121T' appearing in multiple records.

rule: ID_No must not contain obvious test or placeholder values
rationale: Value 'F0000000X' detected with all-zero digit pattern, indicating a test or sentinel entry rather than a valid ID.

rule: Race must be one of: Chinese, Malay, Indian
rationale: Evidence shows 3 semantic categories with case variations (MALAY, malay, indian). Must standardize to canonical Title Case values.

rule: Gender must be either Male or Female
rationale: Evidence shows 2 semantic categories with case inconsistencies (male, FEMALE). Must conform to standard Title Case values.

rule: Age must be numeric and parseable as a number
rationale: Column contains text value 'Twenty-five' which cannot be parsed as numeric. All values must be convertible to numbers.

rule: Age must be between 0 and 120 (inclusive)
rationale: Domain constraint for human age. Flags impossible negative value (-5) and validates upper bound of lifespan.

rule: Contact_No must not be null
rationale: Contact number is a mandatory field for customer communication. Evidence shows 6.7% missing values (2 records) requiring validation.

rule: Contact_No must be a valid Singapore phone number (8 digits, starting with 6, 8, or 9; or with 65 country code prefix)
rationale: Dataset is Singapore-centric. Valid numbers are 8-digit local format or with +65/65 prefix. Flags 7-digit value '8964359' and other malformed entries.

rule: Email must not be null
rationale: Email is a mandatory contact field. No missing values observed in sample.

rule: Email must contain exactly one @ symbol with no whitespace (e.g., user@example.com)
rationale: Evidence shows 4 structurally malformed values: missing @ ('not-an-email', 'useremail.com'), contains space ('zx91 @example.com'), or double @ ('nabilah@@example.com').

rule: Email values must be unique
rationale: Email addresses should uniquely identify customers. Evidence shows duplicate value 'thm@example.com'.

rule: Country must be 'Singapore' (standardized from variants like 'SG', 'S'pore', 'Singapura', '新加坡', 'Republic of Singapore')
rationale: Evidence shows 8 different representations of Singapore. Must standardize to canonical English short form 'Singapore'.

rule: Street_Name must not be in all uppercase (e.g., 'Holland Road' not 'HOLLAND ROAD')
rationale: Evidence shows one all-caps value 'HOLLAND ROAD' deviating from dominant Title Case format used in other 29 records.

rule: Postal_Code must not be null
rationale: Postal code is mandatory for address validation and geographic analysis. No missing values observed.

rule: Postal_Code must contain 4 to 6 digits when represented as string (e.g., 6907, 99999, 410633)
rationale: Evidence indicates intended string type with variable length 4-6 digits. Validates against non-numeric characters after type conversion.

rule: Name particles indicating gender must match the Gender column: Bin/s/o indicate Male; Binte/d/o indicate Female
rationale: Multicultural naming conventions encode gender: Malay 'Bin' (Male) / 'Binte' (Female) and Indian 's/o' (Male) / 'd/o' (Female). Mismatches indicate data inconsistency.

check_params.logic: ((re.search(r'\bBinte\b', str(row['Name']), re.IGNORECASE) or re.search(r'\bd/o\b', str(row['Name']), re.IGNORECASE)) and str(row['Gender']).strip().lower() != 'female') or ((re.search(r'\bBin\b', str(row['Name']), re.IGNORECASE) or re.search(r'\bs/o\b', str(row['Name']), re.IGNORECASE)) and str(row['Gender']).strip().lower() != 'male')

rule: Account_No must match the corresponding Account_No in Acc_Info_dirty for the same S_N
rationale: One-to-one relationship between tables implies Account_No should be consistent across both tables for matching S_N values.

check_params.semantic_check: Account_No values must be identical between Cust_Bio_dirty and Acc_Info_dirty for matching S_N

rule: ID_No must match the corresponding ID in Acc_Info_dirty for the same S_N
rationale: One-to-one relationship requires ID consistency between biographical data and account information tables for the same individual.

check_params.semantic_check: ID_No must match ID in Acc_Info_dirty for matching S_N

rule: Name should match Full_Name in Acc_Info_dirty for the same S_N (allowing for formatting differences)
rationale: One-to-one relationship requires name consistency. Validates that the same individual is represented in both tables, though exact string matching may require case normalization.

check_params.semantic_check: Name must correspond to Full_Name in Acc_Info_dirty for matching S_N
